# A busy App Worker leaves the old focus path marked focused, with no leave

## Context

`manager.Focus` pairs a focusout with the focusin that follows it into one focus move, and it decides the pairing by App-Worker wall-clock time. When the worker is busy for longer than `maxFocusInOutGap` (50 ms) *between* handling the focusout and handling its focusin — a heavy render in between is enough — the move is misread: the focusin becomes a fresh `focusEnter`, and the focusout's pending leave is then suppressed because a focusin "came after" it. No `focusLeave` is ever delivered, and every component on the old path keeps `containsFocus: true` until its own next focus event.

**Observed twice, independently.**
1. `#15536` (2026-07-19, @neo-opus-vega, FM cockpit): a heavier card re-render pushed a same-app focus move to 140 ms, "classified as a fresh focusEnter, which never clears the PRIOR card's containsFocus — so two cards read as focused at once". Worked around at app level in commit `5a9bf47`; the engine was left alone because clearing prior paths on enter would be wrong in multi-window apps. That workaround lived in the since-replaced FleetGrid — `apps/agentos/view/fleet/roster/**` reads no `containsFocus` today.
2. 2026-09-19 (this ticket), a deterministic unit probe on `dev@7db03e862c`: focus on A → `onFocusout(A)` → the thread busy 80 ms → `onFocusin(B)` → wait out the timer. Idle control: A `false`, B `true`. Busy: **A `true`, B `true`**.

Found while writing up @neo-opus-ada's `[KB_GAP]` on PR #18938: the grid editor's reprojection rule reads `view.containsFocus`, and under this defect a click outside the grid while the worker is busy would leave the flag true and let the editor take focus back.

## The Problem

`src/manager/Focus.mjs`:

- `onFocusin` stamps `lastFocusInDate = new Date()` and calls `focusMove` only if `lastFocusInDate - lastFocusOutDate < maxFocusInOutGap`, else `focusEnter`.
- `onFocusout` stamps `lastFocusOutDate = new Date()` and schedules `focusLeave` after the gap, delivered only if `lastFocusOutDate === date && date > lastFocusInDate`.

Both stamps are *processing* times. The browser fires the pair in one main-thread task, so the real gap is ~0 ms. But if the worker handles the focusout, then runs something for more than 50 ms, then handles the focusin before the timer's callback runs, the two tests become complementary in the wrong way: the move test fails (gap too long) and the leave test fails (a focusin is newer). Neither branch fires for the old path.

The DOM events already carry their own `timeStamp` (`main/DomEvents#getEventData`), and `manager.Focus` ignores it — but see Avoided Traps for why that is not the fix.

## The Architectural Reality

- `manager.Focus` (singleton, App Worker) receives `focusin` / `focusout` from `main.DomEvents#onFocusIn` / `#onFocusOut` with `componentPath` (ids upwards) and `data` (`path`, `relatedTarget`, `timeStamp`, and `removedNodeId` for an engine removal).
- `setComponentFocus(opts, flag)` writes `containsFocus` on every component of a path and fires `focusEnter` / `focusLeave` / `focusChange`; `focusMove` diffs the old path (`history[0]`) against the new one at their closest common component.
- The pending leave's guards stay: identity (a newer focusout supersedes an older one's leave) and `isRemovedFloatingShownAgain` (a removed floating component shown again keeps its focus).
- `component.Base#containsFocus_`'s JSDoc says only "manager.Focus will change this flag on focusin & out dom events". It never says what the flag answers — DOM focus inside this component's subtree, never *which* descendant — nor when it changes. Three #18762 leaves misread it within a day (`#18863`'s same-tick read, a retracted defect-note that read it before the round trip, and #18938's in-View gesture).

## The Fix

Pair by **pending state**, not by clock:

- `onFocusout` records its `opts` as the pending focusout and schedules the leave after `maxFocusInOutGap`, as today.
- `onFocusin`: a pending focusout makes the pair a move (and clears the pending one); none makes it an enter.
- The timer delivers the leave only while its focusout is still the pending one, and not for a removed floating component shown again — the existing identity guard, keyed on the pending `opts` instead of a `Date`.
- `lastFocusInDate` / `lastFocusOutDate` retire. Only `test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs`'s `afterEach` reads them, and `lastFocusOutDate`'s docblock names the wrong member.
- `component.Base#containsFocus_` gets a JSDoc that states what it answers and when it changes.
- `maxFocusInOutGap`'s JSDoc says what the gap now bounds: how long a focusout waits for its focusin before it counts as a leave.

In every idle case this is behaviour-identical: a focusin inside the gap was a move and stays one, and a focusout alone still leaves after the gap. Under load the worker never saw an intermediate state, and "a move" is the faithful account of what it knows.

Accretion: no consumer line is deleted — the one workaround (`#15536`) is gone with the grid it lived in. This is a correctness fix for every reader of the flag.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs`: focus on A, a focusout, the thread busy past `maxFocusInOutGap`, a focusin on B, the timer run out → A `false`, B `true`, and A received its leave. RED on `dev`.
- [ ] Every existing `Focus.spec.mjs` arm passes unchanged (superseded focusout, removed floating menu shown again, the three dismissals, the closest-common-component move).
- [ ] Reverting the classification to the clock comparison turns the new arm red.
- [ ] `containsFocus_` states: DOM focus is inside this component's subtree — not which descendant, so focus moving between two descendants that share one focused node (a grid View's cells) never changes it; App-Worker state, set when the worker handles the focusin and cleared one `maxFocusInOutGap` after a focusout unless a focusin pairs it into a move.
- [ ] Unit tier green; component tier green; `e2e/grid/CellEditingReprojectionFocus.spec.mjs` green.

## Out of Scope

- Per-window focus state for multi-window apps. A focusout in one window and a focusin in another can pair today inside the gap, and still can.
- The DOM events' own `timeStamp` (see Avoided Traps).
- Any Neural Link or Brain surface.

## Avoided Traps

- **Compare the DOM events' `timeStamp`.** Each window's `event.timeStamp` counts from its own `performance.timeOrigin`, so two windows of one SharedWorker app stamp on unrelated clocks. It would need an absolute clock in the payload, and it still answers "how far apart" when the question is "are these a pair".
- **Clear every prior path on `focusEnter`.** Rejected in `#15536` and still wrong: in a multi-window app a second window's element legitimately holds focus.
- **Raise `maxFocusInOutGap`.** Moves the threshold only. A render longer than any gap reopens the hole, and a longer gap delays every genuine leave.
